findings.title: Successfully repaired settings still abort the cutover
findings.description: `pg_settings.sh` prints initial `DRIFT` lines before applying changes and reporting their final state. `setup_backup` preserves that output, and `setup_not_ok` rejects every historical drift—even settings subsequently reported `OK`. Consequently, initial tick configuration changes abort step 4 before the restart. Evaluate a fresh check or final per-item status instead, and test an actual drift → applied → OK sequence.

findings.title: Re-running after cron installation always fails
findings.description: Only the new cron lines have their added arguments stripped. On a rerun, `ctx.old_cron` already contains those arguments, so comparing an unchanged post-cutover file against itself reports differences and aborts step 4. This prevents the documented recovery procedure after any later failure. Normalize both sides and add a post-cutover rerun regression test.

findings.title: Failed health commands can pass using an old log
findings.description: `run_health` discards the command result and accepts the existing log’s last summary. If the command fails before appending—for example, because its script is unavailable or its log cannot be written—a previous clean summary can satisfy both health gates. Require evidence that this invocation produced a new summary, while retaining the intentional allowance for stale-only flags during the first check.

findings.title: Ordinary filesystem failures bypass the promised failure report
findings.description: The step runner catches only `StepFailed` and `CalledProcessError`. File reads, `arm.touch()`, and process startup can raise `OSError`; empty logs can raise `IndexError`. These escape before `main` writes the report, potentially after host changes have occurred. Record operational exceptions at the process boundary and ensure report generation runs on failure.
